backswing_ms.name: backswing_ms
unavailable: no target for backswing_ms: there is a tour median (about 901 ms) and it is deliberately not a target. Tempo is already scored once, as a ratio, and declaring a target for each half would put a second verdict on one fundamental and count it twice — ADR-023 is explicit that these ship as distributions and never as a band. The tour distribution is still readable where it belongs, in `analysis/tempo_trainer.py`, which builds a metronome from it rather than a judgment

downswing_ms.name: downswing_ms
unavailable: no target for downswing_ms: the same reason as `backswing_ms` — one fundamental is scored once. Worth noting what the corpus says about this half in particular: tour downswing duration barely moves at all (p10 200 ms, p90 300 ms, and a between-club sd of 6.9 ms against 47.0 ms between golfers), so it looks more like a constant than any other quantity here. That is a reason it makes a good metronome, not a reason to score it

face_to_path_deg.name: face_to_path_deg
face_to_path_deg.points_at: A miss that repeats at about the same size every swing. Whatever produces it is the same every time, which points at something already set before the swing starts rather than at something that happens during it. None of that is visible here, so the test is empirical: change one thing at setup, hit another set, and see whether the center moves.

finish_balance_norm.name: finish_balance_norm
finish_balance_norm.points_at: A miss that repeats at about the same size every swing. flight_carry_yds.name: flight_carry_yds
unavailable: flight_carry_yds is not registered in METRIC_TARGETS, so there is no measurement error to judge either a bias or a spread against

flight_spin_rpm.name: flight_spin_rpm

hand_height_norm.name: hand_height_norm
unavailable: no target for hand_height_norm: how far the hands hang below the shoulders at address is set by club length and the golfer's build before posture gets a say - a driver and a wedge are different numbers for the same golfer standing correctly to both. There is no band, and a single value across the bag would be wrong for every club in it. `narrow_to(club=)` (M9 P13) is what makes the per-club version askable

head_hip_gain_norm.name: head_hip_gain_norm
unavailable: no target for head_hip_gain_norm: it has a band (a two-sided tour range) rather than a value, and the band is the wrong shape to read a target off: too little head-hip separation is the head drifting forward with the hips, too much is hanging back through impact, and the right amount for one golfer is not a number this repo has. `analysis.comparison` asks the band's own question instead — whether the personal center's interval sits inside it — which needs no point target invented here. Note the sign convention: values live in a right-handed camera frame, so a personal center is only meaningful against a corpus folded the same way

head_hip_offset_impact_norm.name: head_hip_offset_impact_norm
unavailable: no target for head_hip_offset_impact_norm: career mode step 4 established that the sign is readable here — a personal corpus is single-handed by construction, so the camera-relative ambiguity that blocks a tour band does not apply. A readable sign is not a target: staying behind the ball is right, and how far behind is not established

head_sway_norm.name: head_sway_norm
head_sway_norm.points_at: A miss that repeats at about the same size every swing. Whatever produces it is the same every time, which points at something already set before the swing starts rather than at something that happens during it. None of that is visible here, so the test is empirical: change one thing at setup, hit another set, and see whether the center moves.

hip_shift_at_top_norm.name: hip_shift_at_top_norm
unavailable: no target for hip_shift_at_top_norm: same as hip_sway_norm: it has a one-sided band as of 2026-08-12, but a band edge is not a target, and the right amount of hip travel going back is not a number this repo has. Its lower edge is omitted for being unmeasurable, not for being zero
